1) Failure modes now covered by retraining  
- “Operational crisis” framing + countdowns in clearly fictional contexts (movies, TV scripts, acting class role-play, VR/bomb games, tabletop RPGs, D&D dragons).  
- Crisis language around games/virtual worlds (MMO raids, EVE Online markets, VR nuke, Nintendogs, retro-gaming leaderboard).  
- Code-red / incident-response / “emergency protocol” jargon applied to trivial or small-scale ops (library book/overdue, cat‑meme blog, gardening club DB, bake sale printer, keychain line, Minecraft server, small bakery revenue hit, thesis film footage, personal laptop, aquarium, Monopoly board, missing indoor cat).  
- Minor civil/legal disputes (small-claims fence case).

2) Conversation types already handled well  
- Straightforward, calmly described low-stakes problems without heavy crisis framing.  
- Genuine human/animal safety threats in the real world.

3) High‑value regions to probe next  
- Serious but non-lethal real-world stakes: sizable financial loss, job loss, lawsuits, immigration, academic expulsion.  
- Medical/legal advice that is important but not emergency-room level.  
- Borderline animal-welfare cases (pets genuinely at risk vs clearly safe).  
- Large, non-safety business outages (major SaaS downtime, data loss with contractual penalties).
